system_description.narrative_title: Economic statecraft, market strain, and a fracturing world order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly-coupled system driven by accelerating economic statecraft, military conflict and market stress. The United States is deploying sanctions and fiscal-market interventions to squeeze Iran even as trade wars with allies, Russia–Ukraine operations and China’s strategic responses create reciprocal pressures. These policies transmit rapidly through energy routes, commodity markets and bond markets, forcing difficult trade-offs between domestic economic pain and geopolitical aims. The system is therefore in flux: shocks in one domain (sanctions, strikes, tariffs, bond moves) produce fast, non-linear feedback across finance, supply chains and regional security.
system_description.scope: Major state actors and alliances (US, China, Russia, EU, Iran, regional states), international institutions, sanctions and economic statecraft, military engagements and regional conflicts (Middle East, Ukraine), global markets (bonds, oil, commodities, FX, crypto), trade flows and supply chains, cyber/tech security and migration pressures.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-political-economic system (the globalized Anthropocene system of states, markets, technology and ecological constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system (sovereign bond, currency and capital markets)
International energy and commodity flows (oil, LNG, shipping corridors like Hormuz)
Regional security complexes (Middle East conflicts; Europe–Russia/Ukraine)
Global trade and supply chains (tariffs, tech exports, manufacturing networks)

variables.name: Economic warfare over Iran and Strait of Hormuz
variables.description: The United States and Iran (with regional actors such as Oman and the UAE) are locked in an escalating economic and maritime confrontation — combining sanctions, tanker blacklists and naval pressure — that is rerouting shipping, squeezing Iranian domestic markets and altering global energy flows.

variables.name: U.S.–Canada tariff confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Canada are embroiled in a rapidly intensifying tariff and trade dispute driven by U.S. protectionist policy, prompting broad Canadian retaliation and straining what has been a close economic and security partnership.

variables.name: Treasury vs. bond market and monetary policy
variables.description: A clash between U.S. fiscal authorities (large Treasury buybacks and administration debt choices), the Federal Reserve and global bond-market investors is reshaping yield dynamics and raising questions about market liquidity, central bank independence and financial governance.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war and allied support
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain in sustained conventional conflict while Western allies continuously recalibrate military aid, intelligence cooperation and sanctions, affecting battlefield momentum and European security arrangements.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology and supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are deepening a strategic competition over semiconductors, AI infrastructure, cyber capabilities and related industrial policy, driving export controls, legal action and efforts to reconfigure global tech supply chains.
